long_biography.plain_text:
The Mine Shaft property in Rancho Cordova became the clearest public expression of Patrick K. Willis's philanthropy when he transferred the building and roughly 12 acres to the Cordova Community Council in 2018. The gift gave the organization a permanent venue for nonprofit activities after years in which Willis had already made the site available for fundraising events.

That local commitment extends to the Boys & Girls Club of El Dorado County. Willis's company and American Recovery Service have supported the club for more than a decade, pairing event sponsorship with practical help for youth programs. Together, the property gift and sustained club partnership show a community role built around durable institutions rather than one-off donations.

uncertainties.detail: Patrick Willis is a common name shared by a prominent former NFL player. The middle initial, Patrick K. Willis Company name, American Recovery Service relationship and source-record ownership context distinguish this record from the athlete. Current and former yacht names were used only to resolve identity and are excluded from both biographies.

The Cordova Community Council says Willis was 16 when he entered repossession work in 1972, implying a 1955 or 1956 birth year depending on the date. A yacht-focused secondary source gives 1956, but no strong source reviewed supplies a precise date, so no birth field is proposed.

Current trade-association material lists Willis as owner, while current California filing summaries list him as a director and secretary and identify another executive as chief executive. Founder is therefore retained as his principal relationship without describing him as the current day-to-day chief executive.

Secondary sources and public property records suggest material real-estate activity, but the public evidence does not quantify it against the recovery business. Service remains the best-supported primary industry.

Searches returned the former NFL player and several unrelated people named Patrick Willis. No personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website reached the exact-identity threshold.
Forbes identifies Willis in a 2021 article but does not maintain a dedicated profile for him. No Forbes social is proposed.

review.notes: Owner-tag consolidation research context: [1] American Recovery Service: American Recovery Service is the nationwide vehicle-recovery, compliance and remarketing platform founded and owned by Willis. [2] Automotive asset-recovery services: Willis's defining business recovers financed vehicles and coordinates the surrounding investigations, compliance and disposition workflow. [3] Automotive entrepreneur: Willis built his principal business around nationwide vehicle repossession, recovery, investigations and remarketing services. [4] Automotive-services entrepreneur: Willis built a nationwide service business supporting vehicle lenders rather than manufacturing or selling automobiles. [5] Business services: American Recovery Service supplies lenders and other clients with integrated recovery, compliance, investigation, vendor-management and remarketing support. [6] Community asset donation: Willis transferred the Mine Shaft building and roughly 12 acres to the Cordova Community Council for continuing nonprofit use. [7] Entrepreneurship through acquisition: Willis acquired the repossession business where he had begun working and used it as the platform for American Recovery Service. [8] Founder-controlled private company: Willis remains identified as owner of the private Patrick K. Willis Company group and founder-chairman of its recovery business. [9] Integrated repossession-service platform: American Recovery Service integrates assignment, investigation, vendor oversight, compliance, recovery and remarketing activities in one nationwide platform. [10] Patrick K. Willis Company: Patrick K. Willis Company is Willis's privately owned parent business above American Recovery Service and related trade names. [11] Repossession compliance services: Willis's platform developed compliance and inspection programmes for a nationwide repossession-vendor network. [12] Skip tracing: Skip tracing and investigations are documented components of Willis's nationwide vehicle-recovery operations. [13] Teenage founder: Willis entered vehicle repossession at 16 and acquired his employer's business by age 19. [14] Vehicle remarketing services: Remarketing recovered vehicles is a documented downstream component of Willis's recovery-service platform.
